html:
SMTO-K8S-0007 — SMTO set aside an incomplete Kubernetes cluster record

GUID: 6486677f-613e-4ebe-9e4c-1bd5579c6dd3
Slug: kubernetes-context-invalid
Domain: K8S · Subsystem: k8s

What happened

  • SMTO keeps a short note of which Kubernetes cluster, namespace and Gateway a conversation used. That note is incomplete, so SMTO won't reuse it. Your cluster and commands weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure this conversation is using the Gateway that has access to the cluster you want. The cluster record is tied to one Gateway, and a different one can't reuse it.
  2. Ask the agent to run a read-only command, such as kubectl get pods, on that cluster and namespace. A fresh successful command creates a complete record to replace the incomplete one.
  3. If this keeps happening, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates for that Gateway. A Gateway on an older or newer build may send cluster records SMTO can't accept.

What success looks like

  • The read-only command succeeds and later Kubernetes steps use the cluster and namespace you expect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit SMTO's saved data files to fix the record.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Kubernetes working-context record was rejected because it lacks its Gateway identity or its setup fields differ from the required set (config_ref, context, namespace, cluster, cluster_identity, config_revision, trust_mode).

What this means

  • The Controller adapter finds missing setup/Gateway data, or public kubeconfig validation rejects a field set different from the required contract. These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.

Why this can happen

  • The Controller adapter finds missing setup/Gateway data, or public kubeconfig validation rejects a field set different from the required contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the returned setup schema and selected Gateway with the supported adapter contract.

How to fix it

  • Rediscover the setup by running a supported read-only kubectl command through the intended Gateway so a fresh receipt replaces the record. If new receipts are rejected too, make sure the Gateway and Server run matching builds (Settings › Setup › Gateways, Check for updates).
  • Rediscover the intended Kubernetes context on the selected Gateway and check the exact cluster and namespace before continuing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh discovery yields a complete accepted setup associated with the intended Gateway.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
